chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him), who said:
When Amir al-Mu'minin (peace of God be upon him) appointed Shurayh as the judge, he stipulated upon him that he would not enforce any judgement until he had first presented it to him.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amir al-Mu'minin — Commander of the Faithful, the title of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him)
key_terms.اشْتَرَطَ: ishtarata — stipulated a condition; placed a binding requirement as a precondition for the appointment
key_terms.الْقَضَاءَ: al-qada' — the judgeship/judicial office; also the act of issuing and enforcing a judicial ruling
key_terms.يُنْفِذَ: yunfidha — to execute/enforce a ruling, putting a decision into binding effect

ai.seo_question: What condition did Imam Ali place on Shurayh when appointing him as judge?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates that Imam Ali (peace be upon him), when appointing the judge Shurayh, placed a condition upon him that no judicial ruling could be enforced without first being reviewed and approved by the Imam. This account is cited in the chapter 'The government, but rather, it is for the Imam' (al-hukumah bal hiya lil-Imam), underscoring the Shia principle that legitimate judicial authority ultimately derives from and remains subordinate to the Imam. In the early Islamic polity, this arrangement meant that the Imam retained supreme oversight over the administration of justice, ensuring that rulings aligned with divine guidance.
